For each cut $k$, let $P_k$ be the orthogonal projection on the full tensor product onto the retained left Schmidt subspace at that cut tensored with the remaining right factors; set $P_0=I$. The current remainder before cut $k$ is $\psi^{(k-1)}=P_{k-1}\psi$. Its support in the first $k$ sites lies in the previous retained space tensored with $H_k$, so every positive left Schmidt vector retained by the next SVD lies in that previous space tensored with $H_k$. Hence $\operatorname{ran}P_k\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P_{k-1}$, $P_kP_{k-1}=P_{k-1}P_k=P_k$, and the next remainder is $\psi^{(k)}=P_k\psi$. [given, F1, F3, construct]
exact_edits.replacement: 1.1 Since $\|\psi\|=1$ and every cap $D_k\ge1$, each current remainder has a positive singular value and the algorithm retains at least one; hence all subsequent remainders are nonzero and all retained bond dimensions are positive. The loop makes one SVD for each $k=1,\ldots,N-1$, exactly $N-1$ in total. Put $\mathcal H_{\le k}:=H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_k$ and $\mathcal R_k:=H_{k+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$, with $\mathcal H_{\le0}=\mathbb C$. Let $U_k:S_k\to S_{k-1}\otimes H_k$ have the retained left singular columns, so $U_k^*U_k=I_{S_k}$ and $\psi^{(k)}=(U_k^*\otimes I_{\mathcal R_k})\psi^{(k-1)}$. Define $W_0=I_{\mathbb C}$ and $W_k=(W_{k-1}\otimes I_{H_k})U_k:S_k\to\mathcal H_{\le k}$. Each $W_k$ is an isometry by induction. Under the canonical $\mathbb C\otimes\mathcal H\cong\mathcal H$ identification, set $x_0=\psi$, $P_0=I$, and, for $k\ge1$, $x_k=(W_k\otimes I_{\mathcal R_k})\psi^{(k)}$ and $P_k=(W_kW_k^*)\otimes I_{\mathcal R_k}$ on the full chain. The range of $W_k$ lies in $\operatorname{ran}W_{k-1}\otimes H_k$, so $\operatorname{ran}P_k\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P_{k-1}$ and $P_kP_{k-1}=P_{k-1}P_k=P_k$. The remainder recurrence gives $x_k=P_kx_{k-1}=P_k\psi$ inductively. Expanding $W_{N-1}$ in the stored site tensors shows that $x_{N-1}$ is exactly their contraction with the final remainder, hence is the returned unnormalized $\phi$ in algorithm instruction 3. For $N=1$, $x_0=\phi=\psi$. [given, F1, F2, F3, construct, algebra]
